Wait, that doesn't make sense. Let me reconsider.

- After click: cross at (16, 14) became G

2. But clicking on a different cross "deselects" the previous one

Let me test this hypothesis: move the target without clicking, and see if the cross color changes.

Let me think about this differently. Maybe the click on (16, 14) changed the cross to G, but then the click on (16, 44) changed it back. This would mean clicking on a cross toggles it, and clicking on a different cross toggles that one too.
But the result shows all 5 crosses are N (green) after the second click. So the click on (16, 44) didn't change (16, 44) to G, and it also reverted (16, 14) back to N.
This is confusing. Let me try clicking on (16, 44) again to see if it toggles.

# Click on (16, 44) again to see if it toggles
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 16, 'col': 45}])

    r = (min(p[0] for p in b) + max(p[0] for p in b)) // 2
    c = (min(p[1] for p in b) + max(p[1] for p in b)) // 2
    print(f"  N at ({r},{c})")
print(f"Dark gray crosses: {len(G_objects)}")
for n in G_objects:
    b = n['boundary']
    r = (min(p[0] for p in b) + max(p[0] for p in b)) // 2
    c = (min(p[1] for p in b) + max(p[1] for p in b)) // 2
    print(f"  G at ({r},{c})")

print(f"Gameplay changed: {last_action_result.get('gameplay_changed')}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
